title: Jude and the Witness
premise: Estate lawyer Dominic Iversen is hired to probate the will of Marisol Vance, a woman whose death was ruled an accident — until a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after her funeral, naming a killer and claiming the will itself is forged. Dominic discovers the letter was written by Jude, Marisol's estranged half-sibling, who witnessed the murder but has spent years hiding under another identity to survive an earlier crime. As the statute of limitations on that old crime nears expiry, the real killer — Marisol's business partner, who memorized every file in the estate — begins erasing evidence and framing Jude. Dominic must choose between handing Jude to the police as bait or running an off-the-books trap; in the climax she baits the killer with a fake codicil, records his confession, and clears Jude's name at the cost of her law license, ending with Jude inheriting the estate and Dominic walking away from the profession that taught her justice only lives inside files.
about_author: Elodie Reyes is a former paralegal from coastal Maine who spent a decade drafting wills for families with more secrets than assets. She writes mysteries about paper trails, quiet witnesses, and the people the legal system forgets.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Dominic Iversen, POV. A week after Marisol Vance's funeral, a lawyer delivers a handwritten will no one knew about, superseding the one already probated. Dominic, who prides herself on closing every case, accepts despite the irregularities. Beat: professional pride masking a first flicker of unease.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Among the estate papers arrives an unsigned confession letter describing Marisol's death in detail only the killer could know — postmarked the day after the funeral. The letter names no one but begs someone to 'read the file twice.' Beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: A House Full of Signatures
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. At the Vance house, Dominic interviews the beneficiaries: business partner Aldous Crane, grieving nephew Theo, and housekeeper Ruth. Everyone's timeline is polished, rehearsed. She notices the original will's witness signatures match documents Crane keeps in his office. Beat: suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: Jude
chapters.summary: Jude, POV (introduced unnamed). A night-shift warehouse worker with a false name watches news coverage of the Vance estate dispute and burns a photograph. We learn Jude wrote the confession letter and once testified — or refused to — in another case years ago. Beat: guilt and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Reading the File Twice
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Following the letter's instruction, Dominic re-examines the accident report and finds the coroner's timeline contradicts Crane's statement by forty minutes. When she requests the full case file, she learns someone else requested it three days ago — using her own firm's letterhead. Beat: the hunter realizes she's being hunted.

chapters.title: What Jude Saw
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Flashback: the night Marisol died, Jude watched from the boathouse as Crane argued with her on the dock; the 'fall' came after. Jude fled rather than testify, because exposure would resurrect an old warrant. Beat: the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Dominic traces the old warrant to a cold case connected to Jude's real identity and realizes the confession writer has twenty-three days before the statute expires — after which their testimony becomes legally worthless. Someone with access to court records knows it too. Beat: urgency becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: Crane's Perfect Memory
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Over a staged negotiation about the estate, Dominic tests Crane with deliberately altered details from the case file; he corrects her errors without hesitation — details never made public. He smiles and offers to settle quickly. Beat: confirmation wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: Theo's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The nephew admits Marisol had planned to dissolve the partnership and rewrite her will days before dying; he shows Dominic a torn draft he hid out of fear. That night someone ransacks his apartment. Beat: collateral damage begins.

chapters.title: Two Letters
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Dominic receives a second letter — this one threatening, warning her to close the estate quietly. Comparing handwriting, she confirms both letters share a hand: the confession and the threat come from different people, meaning the confessor isn't the threatener. Beat: the shape of the trap clarifies.

chapters.title: Finding Jude
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Using the postmark route and a pawnshop receipt tucked in the will's envelope, Dominic finds Jude at the warehouse. Their confrontation is electric: Jude refuses to go to police, convinced the system destroyed them once before. Beat: two survivors negotiating trust.

chapters.title: The Old Warrant
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Jude tells Dominic the whole history: a coerced plea, a dead friend, a name abandoned. Dominic proposes a bargain — Jude's testimony inside a trap Dominic controls, not a courtroom. Jude hesitates, then agrees, keeping one condition: if it fails, Dominic walks away and never looks back. Beat: alliance sealed.

chapters.title: Ruth Knows More
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. The housekeeper reveals Marisol called her the night she died, frightened, asking Ruth to hide a folder. Ruth buried it in the garden shed and has been silent out of fear for her job — and her immigration status. Beat: another survival priced in silence.

chapters.title: The Folder
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. The hidden folder contains proof Crane embezzled from the company and that Marisol discovered it — motive, finally documented. But a page is missing, and Dominic realizes Crane must have known the folder existed all along. Beat: victory curdling into vulnerability.

chapters.title: Someone Inside
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Dominic discovers the firm's junior associate leaked her file requests to Crane — bought off years ago in a case she never questioned. Confronting him, she learns Crane's reach goes further than she imagined, possibly into the police department. Beat: isolation deepens; no institution can be trusted.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. With eight days left on the statute, Jude grows paranoid after a near-miss tailing Crane. Dominic proposes the endgame: forge a codicil claiming Marisol hid a second copy of the embezzlement ledger, and let Crane come for it himself. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bait
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Dominic registers the fake codicil publicly and lets word leak through the compromised associate. She wires the boathouse where Marisol died with recording equipment, betting Crane's vanity and his perfect memory of the file will draw him to destroy it personally. Beat: calm before the storm.

chapters.title: Boathouse
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic/Jude POV. Crane takes the bait, arrives to burn the codicil, and finds Jude waiting — the witness he thought he'd erased. He confesses aloud, believing Jude is alone and disposable. Dominic steps from the dark with the recorder running as Crane lunges. Beat: climax; terror, then reversal.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Heard
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. The recording catches everything — including Dominic admitting she orchestrated a fraudulent codicil. Detective Okafor, the one honest cop, takes Crane into custody but presents Dominic with a choice: testify cleanly and lose her license, or bury the recording's second half. Beat: the price comes due.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Jude testifies under their real name for the first time in fifteen years, the old warrant expiring mid-hearing. The courtroom scene is quiet, undramatic — just a voice that finally says what happened on the dock. Beat: justice inside the law, barely, and hard-won.

chapters.title: Surrender of License
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Dominic pleads guilty to the codicil fraud and surrenders her bar license, refusing to shift blame. Walking out of the courthouse, she passes Crane in cuffs and feels not triumph but lightness. Beat: sacrifice accepted without bitterness.

chapters.title: The Estate Settled
chapters.summary: Dominic and Jude, alternating final sections. Jude inherits the Vance house and opens it to Ruth and Theo; Dominic takes work as an investigator for public defenders. On the dock where Marisol died, they scatter the last of the estate papers to the wind. Beat: resolution — inheritance redefined as what we carry forward.
